Although it is never explicitly said, it is possible to infer that the victory of the Lords over the Ancient Dragons occurred directly thanks to Seath, through him revealing that the weakness of his race was lightning, capable of piercing their stone Dragon Scales. This is because in the Japanese version of the Opening, it is explained how the Lords' victory was "caused" by Seath's betrayal (ウロコのない白竜、シースの裏切りにより、遂に古竜は敗れた TL: And because of the betrayal of the scaleless white dragon Seath, the ancient dragons were finally defeated). This would also explain the immense amount of gifts that Gwyn gave to the white dragon including the Archives of the Gods, a political position in his empire, a woman from his family and a fragment of his Lord's soul.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: At some point, the Four Lords who had found immense Lord Souls and built their civilizations underground emerged to the surface with the intention of waging war against the Dragons and conquering the world for themselves. Seath decided to betray his race to ally with Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight, and help the Lords in the war. He was instrumental in the gods' eventual victory, and the triumphant Lords would exterminate much of the Ancient Dragons, cementing their rule. Seath would also pillage the Ancient Dragons' sacred treasure, the Primordial Crystal, the centerpiece of his efforts to achieve immortality.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Seath the Scaleless -  Dark Souls - boss - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Seath is one of the primordial archdragons who inhabited the world when, before the appearance of the First Flame, the world was composed only of grey rocks.

Seath was born with unique characteristics compared to the other archdragons, lacking the rock scales that made his brethren immortal. In addition, Seath's pale and deformed body was infused with the magical power of moonlight, through the study of which he created weapons that catalyzed it.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: Through their successful alliance against the Everlasting Dragons, Seath became a close friend to the Lord of Sunlight and was amply rewarded for his indispensable contributions to the war. He was wed into Gwyn's family as his son-in-law, inducting him into the nobility of the Gods, and was bestowed the honorific of "Duke". Gwyn further gifted Seath a fragment of his powerful Lord Soul and the Royal Archives, an enormous library towering above Anor Londo, which contained all the knowledge available to the city of the gods, leaving the dragon the freedom to do his own research; in time, the archives became so synonymous with Seath that they became known as "The Duke's Archives" instead.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: Studying the sorceries and knowledge brought to the Archives by the Crystal Sages, Oceiros would find himself walking the same path as Big Hat Logan, one that led to enlightenment only to be followed by madness. The king, in his deep delusions, believed he had to become a dragon himself in order to produce an heir strong enough to link the Flame. His mad plans would find support from Pontiff Sulyvahn, who began experimenting with transforming humans into pale dragons. Despite the large number of failures and abominations that presented only a faded fragment of the dragons' strength, the experiments were eventually successful and Oceiros managed to transform himself into a scaleless dragon resembling Seath, albeit an imperfect and distorted one, even obtaining the sorcery of Seath's crystal breath.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Seath the Scaleless -  Dark Souls - boss - description 
 description : Seath is a large white dragon that lacks scales and has his lower body covered in crystals. He has a smooth torso that is quite humanoid and in place of legs he has several tentacle-like tendrils. He has six blue-violet wings and has long appendices extending from his head.

title: Chosen Undead
snippet:
In The Duke's Archives the Chosen Undead confronts Seath the Scaleless, an albino dragon who betrayed the Ancient Dragons and won Lord Gwyn´s trust. During their first encounter, the Chosen Undead is unable to cause any harm to Seath and is captured. Seath imprisons the Chosen Undead inside his prison tower where the player cannot warp out from. Despite the inconveniences, the Chosen Undead eventually escapes.

Later on, the Chosen Undead learns from Big Hat Logan that Seath is immortal due to an ancient artifact known as the Primordial Crystal, an old relic that Seath stole from the Ancient Dragons. The Chosen Undead then departs to the Crystal Cave, where the artifact lies, and shatters it. This annuls Seath's immortality, allowing the Chosen Undead to slay him.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: At the culmination of his quest, Seath was able to achieve what he had always sought: immortality through the Primordial Crystal. By connecting his body and soul to the powerful crystal, the pale dragon gained insulation from death, so that no mortal blow could affect him and his wounds would close promptly, as long as the crystal was intact. His very breath became a powerful crystal breath that emitted a lethal curse.

title: Dragon
snippet:
Crossbreed Priscilla of the Painted World of Ariamis is possibly the result of the interbreeding of Seath and an unknown woman.

Seath the Scaleless, the albino dragon, allied with Lord Gwyn and turned against the Ancient Dragons: for this he was awarded Dukedom and given a fragment of a great soul. It is implied he has some connection to the creation of the Serpent Soldiers and Serpent Mages in his experiments for immortality, though whether they have any true connection to Dragons is unknown.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Another possible daughter of Seath was Crossbreed Priscilla, a half-dragon hybrid whose dragon attributes are reminiscent of him; as she is outright described as a bastard, she would have been conceived out of wedlock. Priscilla was feared by the other gods and treated as an abomination due to her Lifehunt powers and unnatural origin. Eventually she was drawn away into the cold and lonely Painted World of Ariamis, trapped within a great canvas.

Seath seemingly had little interest in politics or pleasure, choosing to immerse himself in research of the scales of immortality that the ancient dragons possessed but he lacked. His Archives became a magnificent pool of tomes and knowledge, the fruits of Seath's superior wisdom and unsound fixation over achieving the immortality that was denied to him at birth.

title: Timeline
snippet:
----
Seath The Scaleless betrays his kind and reveals dragon scales give dragons their immortality
Gwyn uses lightning to destroy their scales and make them vulnerable
Nito unleashed a miasma of death and disease, rotting the Archtrees and infecting the dragons
Seath steals the Primordial Crystal and swears allegiance to the newcomers
The majority of dragons and most Archtrees are destroyed, save for lesser dragons and several survivors
One such survivor is the Stone Dragon, founder of The Path of the Dragon
Some Dragons are chosen to serve a purpose under Gwyn's new rule: Midir is raised and trained since its young state to serve as a devourer of dark energy, able to carry its duty at the service of light forever while staying (theoretically) uncorrupted

His Moonlight Sword that shone like the brilliant rays of the moon and was born from his white being had become a thing of the oldest legends, rarely spoken of. The smithing techniques of Seath that used souls to create artifacts were preserved by a clan of Crow Demons, though they remembered the dragon only as a white grotesque being that existed in the distant past.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Seath the Scaleless -  Dark Souls - boss - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : By the era of Lothric, Seath was still widely considered the "pale dragon" of legends even by the sorcerers of Vinheim, though his crystal sorceries were all but consigned to legend.

There were some who still upheld Seath's legacy: The Crystal Sages, twin scholars who considered themselves the spiritual successors of the legendary grand sage Logan, came to possess the Crystal Scroll containing the sorceries and research of the pale dragon, which lead to Logan's records of Crystal Sorcery. The two sages were thus able to carry on this branch of sorcery, allowing them to replicate Logan's discoveries that utilize the power of crystals to their fullest as a medium for souls thanks to his "enlightenment" in the Regal Archives of Seath.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:

Regardless, the player must be killed by Seath in order to progress.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Seath the Scaleless -  Dark Souls - boss - lead 
 lead : , also known as **Duke Seath**, is a boss in *Dark Souls*. He is also a mentioned character in *Dark Souls II*, albeit only as the "**Paledrake**", and a mentioned character in *Dark Souls III*.

One of four great beings who must be slain in *Dark Souls* so that their special souls may satiate the Lordvessel, he uniquely has two distinct boss battles, each with a different location and moveset. In another unique occurence, the first one atop The Duke's Archives must result in the player's death for the game to progress, while he can actually be defeated in his true boss battle at the end of the Crystal Cave.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: infestation with satisfaction. The spider haunted by Seath thus returned to the depths of the mines next to the petrified body of the ancient dragon and began to accumulate the souls gathered in the lands of Tseldora, absorbing them from people until they grew immensely. Though Freja was ultimately slain, Tark was doubtful it would be the end of Seath.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
The pale dragon's experiments were successful in animating Crystal Golems with souls and infusing Undead Soldiers with crystals. To adequately supply his research, the cave that housed his Primordial Crystal was gradually crowded with crystals, nearly overtaking the Archive's inner gardens. Seath also created the soul of the Moonlight Butterflies, mystical creatures that emitted crystallic power and Seath's moonlight as sorceries. Seath also managed to crystallize his own magical power of moonlight, creating a Greatsword that catalyzed it.

As a nobleman on par with the gods, Seath also had personal servants. His Channelers, trained sorcerers that became his eyes, hands, and feet, would reach and see what the dragon could not, and helped him in his research. The Channelers wore outfits representing Seath, with the six eyes on their helms meant to "compensate for Seath's lack of sight"; the nature of his lack of sight, and when he became impaired, are unknown.

title: Souls of Lords
snippet:
Soul of one of the Four Kings, who fell to the Dark. A fragment of a Lord Soul discovered at the dawn of the Age of Fire.

Lord Gwyn recognized the foresight of these four great leaders of New Londo, and granted them their ranks and the fragments of a great soul. Although this is not a full Lord Soul, it can still satiate the Lordvessel.

Soul of the albino dragon, Seath the Scaleless. A fragment of a Lord Soul discovered at the dawn of the Age of Fire.

Seath allied with Lord Gwyn and turned upon the dragons; for this he was awarded Dukedom embraced by the royalty, and given a fragment of a great soul. Although just a piece, it will still satiate the Lordvessel.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: Following the death of their creator, multiple moon butterflies survived over the centuries, migrating to Drangleic and mutating into lesser Great Moths and developing poisoning abilities. They remained rare and mysterious creatures that appeared only on full-moon nights in winter, and whose larvae were never once spotted. Other creations of Seath that reached Drangleic included Manscorpion Tark and Scorpioness Najka: Two of Seath's many experiments on humans, the pale dragon's crossbreeding experiments had seemingly cursed their souls into being together. The two were well aware of being the product of Seath's madness and his obsessive attempt to achieve immortality.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
The ghostly hands that emerge from the tomes in the Grand Archives in *Dark Souls III* closely resemble those of Seath; not only visually, but also functionally, as they cause curse build-up in those who come too close, similar to Seath's Curse Beam attacks.
Seath's character is an homage to the dragon god of the same name in FromSoftware's King's Field series for the original Playstation. The Souls series is often referred to as the spiritual successor to King's Field.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Equipment load under 25% is highly recommended to cut his tail.
Lure Seath as close as possible to the crystal. It is ideal to kite Seath close to one of the walls, so that when he attacks with his breath, you have plenty of room to move around his other side. Once Seath is close enough to you he will pause and begin his breath attack; immediately run behind Seath. Run to his left side (your right), as he breathes his crystal breath from his right to his left. Seath will destroy the crystal with his own breath attack and be stunned temporarily. Without locking on to him, target the tip of his back (middle) tail and attack it while two-handing your highest damage weapon or using fast strong spells.
Use weapons that have vertical slash when two-handed: katanas, straightswords, greatswords, ultra greatswords, etc. Slash the tip once or twice, then run away. Provoke him to attack with his crystal breath, run to his tail, slash once or twice again, then repeat.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet: maidens of Gwynevere, before Seath's experiments transformed them. Although Gwyndolin, as the last remaining deity in Anor Londo, did not punish him for this heinous act, Seath was confined to his Archives, declared a forbidden area and demarcated by a divine magical barrier, so that no one could approach the Archives. Meanwhile his Channelers, steadfast in their service of the Duke, continued their travels, kidnapping subjects for his experiments.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Being the grandfather of Sorcery, Seath is extremely resistant to Magic damage, so it would be wise to try to use a different element when combating him.

When trying to obtain the Moonlight Greatsword it is best to attack the tip of the tail, as the area around midway through the tail is considered his body. Thus dealing damage to this area will not help in acquiring the Moonlight Greatsword.

A good strategy for acquiring it is when Seath himself breaks the Primordial Crystal. Wait behind the crystal until Seath starts to rear up his head for any of the Curse Beam attacks. Just before he fires it, start sprinting left or right around the sides and towards his tail. Seath will break the crystal and stun himself, giving the player ample opportunity to attack his tail three to four times. Make sure Seath's tail isn't clipping in the wall before trying.

title: Seath the Scaleless
snippet:
Seath eventually sired a humanoid hybrid daughter, Shira. Although the mother is never stated explicitly, Shira is both "one whose veins coarse with royal blood", and a "descendant of Gods", making her likely mother Seath's spouse who was a relative of Gwyn.
 Shira became the sworn knight and personal handmaiden to Princess Filianore, Gwyn's last daughter, and the two, together with the dragon Darkeater Midir, would be forever sent away to the Ringed City, the hidden city Gwyn gifted to the humans who helped him end the Age of Ancients, so that the three would keep the Dark within at bay. Shira would remain in the Ringed City for the rest of her life, dutifully guarding Filianore over countless ages, although she would always take pride in being Seath's daughter.

title: Dragon
snippet:
The tide was turned when Seath the Scaleless betrayed his own kind, and sided with the Lords. For this he was awarded Dukedom, embraced by the royalty, and given a fragment of a great soul. Seath had been born deformed, and lacked the stone scales that gave his brethren their immortality. He is also is considered the grandfather of sorcery.

The Lords were successful, and claimed dominion of the world.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: The tide would turn in the Lords' favor when Seath, a pale dragon born without the scales of his kind, betrayed the dragons to ally with Gwyn, and pillaged their Primordial Crystal. Seath's lack of scales coupled with his vulnerability provided the Lords with a key piece of information: that the scales of his brethren were the source of their immortality. Gwyn thus used his Great Soul to manipulate the light of the sun, transforming rays of sunlight into lightning, a form of energy capable of penetrating dragon scales. Meeting the dragons in battle, Gwyn used his spears of sunlight to peel apart the dragons' scales, while his knights employed lightning-infused weapons to similar effect. The Witch of Izalith and her daughters weaved great firestorms, destroying the archtrees and burning the dragons; while Nito unleashed a miasma of death, rotting the archtrees and infecting the dragons. Gwyn's eldest son would also take part in the war with his father, killing several dragons with his

title: The Nameless King
snippet: inside the walls of Anor Londo. Furthermore, in the city of the gods Seath the Scaleless had now completely lost his mind, transforming his Archives into a prison and going so far as to kidnap the maidens of Gwynevere to carry out experiments on them.

title: Dragon
snippet:
According to interviews with Miyazaki, the Ancient Dragons are half-living, half-element, and do not feel pain due to them being "beyond human understanding". They are mineral-based lifeforms existing since before humanity's emergence, yet the very emergence of life was capable of corrupting them and causing them to be warped by emotions and desires, to the point where their very bodies adapt and retrogress in pursuit of their survival, such as the Gaping Dragon being warped by greed and the desire to eat.

Seath and the Stone Dragon prove that these beings were capable of higher reasoning and could understand other species' language to at least some degree, via their known contributions to the world (the former, Seath, being the founder of soul sorcery, along with creating the techniques of forging weapons from powerful souls according to Weaponsmith Ornifex).

It is common for the tails of Dragons to be cut off and used in the forging of powerful weapons.

title: Lords
snippet:
Lords -  Dark Souls II - character - aftermath 
 aftermath : Seath was driven to madness as a result of his experiments and accrued knowledge. His attendants would kidnap humans from across the land to be experimented on and even the maidens of Gwynevere. Eventually he discovered a kind of immortality, being invincible so long as the crystal remained. Through the knowledge accumulated by Seath, the human sorcerer Logan would be able to craft new spells and further augment his own spells, though he too would be driven mad much like Seath was.

At some point the Gwyn's firstborn betrayed the gods and allied with the descendants of the dragons, and his name was stripped from him, being removed from all recorded history such as annals and statues.

title: Dragon
snippet: Oceiros, the Consumed King, was formerly the King of Lothric, later becoming obsessed with Seath the Scaleless' work and seeking to become more powerful using his royal blood. With the aid of the scholars of the Grand Archives, he discovered the research made by Logan, who himself was inspired by Seath. Much like Logan, Oceiros was driven insane by the work of the paledrake and somehow transformed into a malformed abomination, somewhat reminiscent of Seath. He has survived many assassination attempts, which he claims is due to the divine protection of the dragon scale.

title: Gods
snippet:
Havel the Rock, a battlefield compatriot of Gwyn who fought at his side against the Everlasting Dragons and inspired many warriors who wore similar equipment. He is referred to as a "bishop" , and is clearly part of the faith of the Way of White, as there were even "priests of Havel" and miracles recalling his tales, although whether he was actually deified, or part of Gwyn's species, is unclear.
Seath, an Everlasting Dragon who sided with Gwyn against his own species. After the war, he was granted Dukedom, married a woman in Gwyn's family, and came to be regarded as the Godfather of sorcery, although he was seemingly not deified.
Many Silver Knights since the Age of Ancients served Lord Gwyn and the other Old Gods of Anor Londo, well into the events of *Dark Souls III*. Their origins and species are never clearly explained.

title: Old Ones
snippet: The Writhing Ruin is described as an ancient entity whose influence in Brightstone Cove Tseldora made the inhabitants be consumed in the search for “that which they lacked”. Furthermore, Manscorpion Tark, who congratulates the player for “defeating his master” after Freja is killed (referring to the Writhing Ruin possesing her) describes his master as a being “born with a fatal flaw, hateful of those that had what he lacked, creator of strange creatures and eroded by solitude and madness". This is a perfect definition of Seath the Scaleless search for immortality. Other correlations are Scorpioness Najka, who has the same creator of Tark, being able to use sorceries, the same crystal theme aesthetic both the Writhing Ruin and Seath have and that the word “Writhing” means a squirming cortorcion similar to the movements of tentacles.

title: Dragon
snippet: The Dragons' iconic characteristic, their stone scales that gave them immortality, was implied to have a strong connection with their own form to the point where Dragons and their scales were considered "inseparable", though the exact truth of this is undetermined. However, their transcendent apostles, who seek the perpetuity of the ancient dragons, have crossed the very ends of the earth to find them and offer them up to rise above their petty corporeal existence and become Dragons. Touching a Ancient Dragon Scale is said to give a person a glimpse into the abyss.

title: Old Ones
snippet:
However, Tark elaborates that his master never dies, only changes form over time and Sweet Shalquoir recalls “that awful traitor long ago who coveted what he did not have …The Writhing Ruin keeps searching as we speak”, this all heavily implies that the Writhing Ruin actually is Seath himself.

The Duke's Dear Freja, from NG+ onward, drops the Old Paledrake Soul.

title: Man Serpent (Lore)
snippet: Ultimately, they might simply be the result of various experiments related to dragons or the Man Serpents, either conducted by Seath himself, who wasn't unfamiliar with merging two different beings together to further his research as evidenced by the existence of Manscorpion Tark and Scorpioness Najka, or by the Bastille Lord himself, their former master.

title: Ocelotte
snippet: In his later years, now consumed by his continuous failures, Oceiros became fascinated by dragons and began to slide into madness, eventually turning to the cursed knowledge of the Grand Archives where he founded the heretical faith in the white dragon Seath. Continuing to study the sorceries and knowledge contained in the Archives and brought by the Crystal Sages to Lothric, Oceiros found himself walking the same path as Big Hat Logan, reaching the same level of "enlightenment" as him and then going completely mad. The king, in his deep delusions, believed he had to become a dragon himself in order to produce an heir strong enough to link the Flame. Oceiros eventually managed to transform himself into a scaleless dragon form, albeit an imperfect and distorted one, even obtaining the sorcery of Seath's crystal breath

title: Lothric
snippet: In his later years, dismayed by failures to find a worthy Champion, Oceiros developed a fascination for dragons that sent him into his descent into madness, eventually turning to the cursed knowledge of the Grand Archives. Here Oceiros found the heretical worship of the white dragon Seath, becoming deeply engrossed in it to the point where he wore a dragonscale ring and had his army use shields decorated with a "white dragon", while giving his royal guard magic rings that enhanced sorcery. By now lost in his madness, Oceiros became known as the "Consumed King"; many assassins were sent to kill him to remove him from power, but he managed to ward off the threat, attributing his salvation to the divine protection of the dragon scale.

A dragon is inseparable from its scales, and the transcendent apostles, who seek the perpetuity of the ancient dragons, have crossed the very end of the earth to seek this invaluable treasure.

title: Lore
snippet:
Soon after, the deities began leaving Lordran. Gwyndolin was the only one of Gwyn's children to stay behind...

Seath, who became obsessed with his research and experiments, amassed countless tomes and was eventually driven mad - at least, how normal people see it - by his research, becoming the founder of sorcery.

At least a thousand years pass and the events of "Dark Souls" begin to unfold...

title: Primordial Serpents
snippet:
Kaathe resides in the darkness of the Abyss, but seems to be more involved in the affairs of Lordran than Frampt. Kaathe gave the Four Kings the art of lifedrain and consequently founded the Darkwraith covenant. He also seems to have tricked the residents of Oolacile into uncovering the corpse of Manus, driving him mad in the process. This sparked the spread of the Abyss, transforming the townsfolk into monstrous beings whose humanity has run wild, akin to Manus.

In the ending of Dark Lord, ten additional primordial serpents are seen, whose names are unknown. They appear to want to serve the newly-appointed Dark Lord, and possibly usher in the Age of Dark. An interesting note in this ending is that Kaathe states that both himself and Frampt will serve the Chosen Undead, disregarding any actions the player has taken before reaching this point, like placing the Lordvessel with Frampt instead of Kaathe, which would make the latter refuse to cooperate with the player, and vice-versa.

title: Lore
snippet:
Lore -  Dark Souls - storyline - the_war_of_fire 
 the_war_of_fire : With their new found power the Lords challenged the dominion of the Everlasting Dragons over the World. The Lords allied with one of the dragons, Seath the Scaleless, who sought the immortal scales of the dragons and thus betrayed his own kind. A very long and destructive war was begun by the Lords and their amassed armies. Gwyn used his powerful bolts to peel their stone scales, while the Witch of Izalith and her Daughters of Chaos wove great firestorms against them and finally the Gravelord Nito unleashed a miasma of death upon the dragons. The war was won by the Lords and the dragons were defeated. A golden Age of Fire begun as the World rebuilt under the new rule of the now as deities perceived Lords.

title: Dragonslayer Armour
snippet: The old knights of Lothric also turned to the Firstborn of Lord Gwyn for aid, once venerated as a god of war and the sun, who in turn gave them the tools to face the wyverns. From the sun god they would learn how to infuse their weapons with the power of lightning, lethal against dragons, and the ancient techniques for hunting archdragons developed in the war between the gods and the Everlasting Dragons. They also learned of his miracles on manipulating lightning as a weapon.

title: Dragon
snippet: description : The Dragons have a few different names throughout the series; **Everlasting Dragons**, **Ancient Dragons**, **Archdragons**, or simply **Dragons**. From what can be glimpsed in the opening, the Everlasting Dragons were towering beings with a skin covered both by stone scales and bristly dark fur. Their head sported two straight horns and a mouth bearing two rows of sharp teeth on both jaws. Their back ended in a long and heavy tail but they were still able to fly thanks to their wings (which often came in two pairs), leathery and clawed like those of a bat. Appropriately for creatures that lived in a world of fog and penumbra, their two eyes had vertical slotted pupils (this kind of eye is the symbol of both the Path of the Dragon and the Dragon Remnants). Aside from these reptilian features, the Everlasting Dragons' body was a lot less bestial than that of their descendants and kin: their arms didn't end in claws but in four-digited prehensile hands while their torso,

title: Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard

Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard -  Dark Souls - item - availability

title: Dragon
snippet:
It is common for the tails of Dragons to be cut off and used in the forging of powerful weapons.

Although the Dragons predate souls and originally did not bear them, over time some would come to possess souls of their own such as Sinh, the Slumbering Dragon, even ones that existed and died just after the Age of Ancients such as the Ancient Dragon. In fact, dragon bones, when imbued with the power of the soul, can be used as an appropriate core to powerful constructs like the Iron Golem, who guards Sen's Fortress and slays the countless heroes seeking Anor Londo. Petrified Dragon Bone is said to house great power.

A Dragon Tooth from an Everlasting Dragon is considered harder than stone and as solid as a boulder, and stated to never break; Havel the Rock would use one as a great club. Merely holding one will grant the user resistance to both fire and magic, suggesting that the Everlasting Dragons had a similar if greater resistance, in contrast to their weakness to lightning.

title: Undead Dragon
snippet:
Undead Dragon -  Dark Souls - enemy - trivia 
 trivia : In an interview with **PlayStation.blog**, Miyazaki said that the Dragon Zombie was designed as one of few survivor of the ancient dragons that went mad".
It's unclear why these dragons are undead, as the Curse of the Undead normally affects only humans. They may be "survivors" of the war against the Everlasting Dragons, reanimated unintentionally by Nito's deadly plague, or kept "alive" by Dragons' inborn vitality.

title: Shira, Knight of Filianore
snippet:
Shira, Knight of Filianore -  Dark Souls III - character - theories 
 theories : It is incredibly likely that the Duke mentioned by Shira is none other than Seath the Scaleless himself. For one, he is the only prominent duke who is ever mentioned as part of the age of the gods, which would explain why Shira speaks of her parentage to a duke as if it were self-explanatory. Another clue may come from the pearl lodged in her crown, which was harvested from the Man Eater Clams. These creatures were found nesting in the Crystal Cave, part of Seath's domain, as well as the primordial Ash Lake, a place tied to the dragons.

title: Dragon
snippet:
Hydras, given their reptilian appearance, breath attacks, and dropping Dragon Scales upon death, are implied to also be descendants of the ancient dragons.

The area boss of the Depths is the Gaping Dragon, a distant, warped descendant of the Everlasting Dragons.

In Ash Lake, the Stone Dragon, a descendant of the ancient dragons, initiates the player into the Path of the Dragon Covenant. Domhnall of Zena shares a rumor that the Stone Dragon is not a descendant and is instead, a surviving Ancient Dragon.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan soon leaves Firelink Shrine after the Lordvessel has been obtained. He is then jailed in The Duke's Archives. Logan explains that he is there to study Seath the Scaleless and his magic. After freeing him with the Archive Tower Giant Cell Key, players can find Logan in an ancillary library close to the third bonfire in The Duke's Archives, where he sells Crystal Sorceries as well as his prior spells. Alternatively, if not freed by you by Seath's defeat, he will free himself and move to the library.

Unfortunately, Logan's infatuation with Seath's magic eventually drives him insane after Seath has been defeated and his entire stock of spells has been purchased. Speaking with him again, after the above conditions are met, will cause him to move to the large chamber where Seath the Scaleless was first encountered and become hostile.

title: Age of Ancients
snippet: theories : It is possible that the humanoid creatures that emerged underground and found the four Lord Souls are an evolution of the dragons over countless years. In fact, after the appearance of the First Flame and the souls, life became possible. The primordial immortal dragons began to mutate like Seath the Scaleless and Black Dragon Kalameet, and reproduced and evolved into different creatures with different characteristics and appearances such as wyverns and serpents. In the depths of the Tomb of the Giants it is in fact possible to find Skeletal Beasts: giant skeletons with bestial behavior that walk on four legs, with in particular a small tail at the end of their spinal column. In these primordial catacombs there are also Giant Skeletons that are able to walk upright and use weapons, but retaining traces of a tail in their bones. These two specimens highlight how those who inhabited the catacombs in very ancient times were creatures initially similar to beasts with tails
